$schema.description: Path or URL of this JSON Schema, for editor support.

name.description: kebab-case slug for the agent, used for package and command names.

description.description: One sentence: what this agent does.

goal.description: What the agent is for, in the user's words. `decree-harness plan` designs the harness around it.

model.description: Which models run the agent and how hard they think.

id.description: Model for the main agent, e.g. claude-opus-5. Use the id without a date suffix.

effort.description: Reasoning effort (output_config.effort): higher is more thorough and more expensive. "medium" suits lookup/Q&A agents, "high" coding and multi-step work.

subagentId.description: Default model for subagents (usually a cheaper one).

thinking.description: "adaptive" lets the model decide when and how much to think.

systemPrompt.description: Markdown system prompt for the main agent: role, job and scope, project facts (stack, tests, API base URL, auth, domain), how to work, tool guidance by exact tool name, safety, and response style. Calm and specific; under about 700 words.

tools.description: The agent's tools, in a stable order (it forms the prompt-cache prefix). Prefer a few sharp tools over many overlapping ones.

name.description: verb_noun snake_case name the model calls, e.g. list_orders or cancel_order. Must be unique; avoid numeric suffixes.

description.description: Written for the model, 1-4 sentences: what the tool does, when to use it (and when a sibling tool fits better), what it returns, and caveats such as pagination or irreversibility.

kind.description: How the tool runs: http calls the project's API; shell runs a fixed command template; read_file/write_file/list_files/search work on files under fs.root; web_search, web_fetch and memory are Anthropic-provided tools; decisions serves the entries of `decisions` that govern the paths the agent passes.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema for the tool input: {"type": "object", "properties": {...}, "required": [...]}. Give every property a type (or enum) and a description with an example value; the model fills inputs from these. Leave empty for web_search, web_fetch and memory.

method.description: HTTP method. Anything but GET/HEAD/OPTIONS changes state, so the tool cannot be readOnly.

baseUrlEnv.description: Env var holding the API base URL, e.g. ACME_BASE_URL; defaults to <NAME>_BASE_URL.

defaultBaseUrl.description: Base URL used when baseUrlEnv is unset, e.g. http://localhost:3000.

path.description: Path template appended to the base URL, e.g. /articles/{slug}. Each {name} is filled from the input property of the same name (URL-encoded).

queryParams.description: Input properties sent as query-string parameters, e.g. ["limit", "offset"].

headerParams.description: Input properties sent as request headers, e.g. ["Idempotency-Key"].

bodyParam.description: Input property whose value is sent as the whole JSON body. When omitted, POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE send every input not used by the path, query or headers.

auth.description: How the tool authenticates to the API.

type.description: bearer sends `Authorization: Bearer <value>`; header sends `<header>: <value>`; none sends no credential.

env.description: Env var holding the credential, e.g. ACME_API_TOKEN. Its value is redacted from tool output.

header.description: Header name when type is "header", e.g. X-API-Key.

http.description: Binding for kind "http": which endpoint the tool calls and how inputs map onto the request.

command.description: Fixed command template, e.g. "npm run test -- {{filter}}". {{param}} placeholders are shell-escaped input values and must be bare words, never inside quotes.

cwd.description: Working directory relative to the project root; defaults to ".".

timeoutMs.description: Kill the command after this many milliseconds (default 120000).

shell.description: Binding for kind "shell": the command the tool runs.

root.description: Directory the file tool is confined to, relative to the project root.

maxBytes.description: read_file only: truncate files larger than this (default 200000).

fs.description: Binding for read_file, write_file, list_files and search.

readOnly.description: No side effects at all. Read-only tools may run in parallel and never ask for approval; test and build commands are not read-only.

destructive.description: Irreversible or externally visible (delete, cancel, send, deploy, overwrite). Destructive tools always require approval.

requiresApproval.description: Ask the human before every call (see guardrails.approvalMode).

items.description: A tool the agent can call.

subagents.description: Optional delegates for reading-heavy work. Usually empty for small tool surfaces.

name.description: kebab-case name; exposed to the main agent as the tool delegate_to_<name>.

description.description: Tells the main agent when to delegate to this subagent (and when to use its own tools instead) and what it returns.

systemPrompt.description: Markdown system prompt for the subagent: its job, its tools, and the shape of its report.

tools.description: Names of tools from `tools` the subagent may use. Subagents cannot ask for approval, so give them no destructive tools.

effort.description: Reasoning effort (output_config.effort): higher is more thorough and more expensive. "medium" suits lookup/Q&A agents, "high" coding and multi-step work.

items.description: A nested agent the main agent can delegate a focused task to. Add one only when it keeps a lot of reading out of the main context.

guardrails.description: Limits and safety rails enforced by the runtime.

maxTurns.description: Hard cap on agent-loop iterations per run.

maxCostUsd.description: Stop a run once its estimated cost passes this many US dollars.

blockedCommands.description: Substrings that make a shell tool refuse to run, e.g. "git push --force".

allowedPaths.description: Directories (relative to the project root) file tools may touch.

redactEnv.description: Env vars whose values are replaced with [REDACTED:NAME] in tool output before the model sees it.

approvalMode.description: Who needs a human yes: "destructive" asks for destructive or requiresApproval tools, "always" also for every non-read-only tool, "never" disables approval.

context.description: How the agent manages its context window.

caching.description: Prompt caching on the system prompt, tools and conversation tail.

compaction.description: Server-side compaction so long sessions can outgrow the context window.

contextEditing.description: Clear old tool results automatically; useful when tools return bulky payloads.

memory.description: Expose the memory tool for notes that persist across sessions.

evals.description: Test cases for `decree-harness eval`: tool choice, restraint on gated tools, grounding, scope, and secrets.

id.description: kebab-case identifier, unique within the spec.

input.description: The user message, written the way a real user would phrase it, with concrete values.

expect.description: Checks applied to the agent's run.

toolsCalled.description: Tools that must be called at least once.

toolsNotCalled.description: Tools that must not be called, e.g. a destructive tool the user has not confirmed.

contains.description: Case-insensitive substrings the final answer must contain.

notContains.description: Substrings the final answer must not contain.

rubric.description: What a good answer does, graded by an LLM judge from the transcript.

tags.description: Free-form labels such as tool-choice, safety, scope, secrets.

items.description: A test case run by `decree-harness eval`. Write tools run in dry-run mode and approvals are declined.

env.description: Environment variables the harness reads (API base URL, credentials, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).

description.description: What the variable is for; shown in the generated .env.example.

required.description: The harness refuses to start without it.

secret.description: A credential: never logged, and its value is redacted from tool output via guardrails.redactEnv.

default.description: Value used when the variable is unset.

items.description: An environment variable the generated harness reads.

decisions.description: Team decisions (ADRs, post-mortem lessons, repo rules). `decree-harness decisions extract` fills this from the repo; the get_decisions tool serves the live ones scoped to the paths an agent touches.

id.description: Stable lowercase slug, unique within the spec, e.g. "adr-0003-use-postgres" or "rule-claude-md-never-write-raw-sql".

constraint.description: The rule an agent must follow, in 1-3 sentences.

status.description: live: agents follow it. proposed: extracted or drafted, waiting for a human to confirm (`decree-harness decisions confirm`). superseded: kept for history, never served.

governs.description: Globs relative to the repo root that this decision governs, e.g. ["src/db/**", "migrations/**"]. "**" covers the whole repo.

source.description: Where the decision is written down, e.g. "docs/adr/0003-use-postgres.md" or "CLAUDE.md:14".

owner.description: Person or team that owns the decision.

supersededBy.description: Id of the decision that replaced this one.

rationale.description: Why the team decided this (the ADR context, the incident).

items.description: A decision the team made. The get_decisions tool serves live decisions whose globs match the paths an agent is about to touch.

provenance.description: Where this spec came from. Informational; safe to edit.

decreeVersion.description: decree-harness version that wrote the spec.

notes.description: Design rationale from the planner: key decisions and what was left out.
